subject: Recap + next steps: PayGrid model fit evaluation
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Evan Hughes <evan@paygrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-16T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Recap + next steps: PayGrid model fit evaluation

Hi Evan / Sara 

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have the same plan: 

Summary of needs
- High throughput question-answering for payments UX (short responses, strict factuality)
- Latency SLO: 200300ms p95 for 256-token requests
- Cost sensitivity: target <$0.0015 per generated token equivalent
- Regulatory note: logs retained for 90 days, see SOC2 evidence request in followup

Recommended initial evaluation plan
1) Models to evaluate (open vs Redwood baseline):
   - Open candidates: Llama-2-13B (q4_0), Mistral-7B-Instruct (w/ 8-bit quant), MPT-7B-Instruct
   - Redwood proprietary baseline: redwood-prod-v1 (our tuned low-hallucination variant)

2) Datasets and prompts
   - Attached: paygrid_prompt_set_v1.json (200 representative prompts across payments flows)
   - We will run both accuracy and hallucination checks against the provided golden answers + synthetic edge cases

3) Acceptance / parity thresholds (proposed)
   - Accuracy (top-1 intent match) within 3% of redwood-prod-v1 on key prompt subset
   - Hallucination rate under 0.5% on factual checks (we flag any hallucinations for review)
   - Latency within your 200300ms p95 SLO for production config (we will test both small and burst QPS)

4) Timeline & deliverables
   - Redwood runs evals on our infra for 3 business days after we get the prompt set + sample logs (we can run on your data in a dedicated tenant if needed)
   - Deliverable: benchmark PDF (latency/cost/accuracy) + a short parity recommendation note

5) Next meeting
   - Proposed: Wed 11/19 10:00am PT to review results and discuss rollout options (hosted vs dedicated)

Attachments: paygrid_prompt_set_v1.json, paygrid_model_benchmarks.pdf (placeholder  final bench will be uploaded after the run)

Open questions for you
- Do you have a preferred acceptance threshold tighter than the 3% accuracy delta?
- Any constraints on test data residency (need to know if we should run in a dedicated tenant)?

I'll kick off the internal eval once you confirm and send the sample logs.

Cheers,
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
lauren@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0192

--
Redwood Inference | Make inference predictable and economical

From: Evan Hughes <evan@paygrid.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Lin <sara@paygrid.com>
Date: 2026-11-16T12:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: PayGrid model fit evaluation

Got it  thanks Lauren. That all sounds reasonable. A few clarifications: 

- The 3% accuracy delta seems fine as a starting point. Internally, our product team would be much happier if we saw <2% delta but we can start with 3% and tighten if early signals are promising.
- For test data: we can provide a 2k-row sample of anonymized production logs (sanitized IDs)  we prefer Redwood to run in a dedicated tenant for the run (data residency).
- Do you have a rough cost estimate for running the eval (compute + token cost) so I can flag to procurement?

Also, we'll need an itemized output we can share with our security team (SOC2 artifacts + model lineage). If possible, include the kernel/quantization profile used for each open candidate in the benchmark.

Happy to confirm the 11/19 slot  Sara & I can do 10am PT.

Thanks,
Evan Hughes
Head of Product, PayGrid
evan@paygrid.com

--

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Evan Hughes <evan@paygrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-17T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: PayGrid model fit evaluation

Thanks for the quick reply, Evan  appreciate the flexibility on thresholds. A few notes that address your asks: 

1) Cost estimate for the eval run
- We estimate the 3-day evaluation (all three open candidates + redwood-prod-v1, ~2k sample inputs, 3-shot prompts where applicable) to cost roughly $1,2001,600 in compute on our infra (this includes GPU time + storage for logs). We'll itemize the breakdown in the benchmark PDF.

2) Security / compliance artifacts
- We'll include SOC2 evidence links, model lineage (model fingerprint + quantization profile), and an exportable audit log for the run. If you need an external-facing report for procurement, we can provide a redacted version.

3) Data residency
- Running in a dedicated tenant is fine  we can provision within your required region and apply your retention policy (90 days). Please attach the sanitized logs to the HubSpot deal or share via the Drive link in your reply.

4) Acceptance thresholds
- We'll run the initial pass at 3% accuracy delta and produce a parity report with per-prompt deltas so your team can decide where to tighten.

Action items
- Evan: share sanitized sample logs + confirm dedicated tenant (reply here)
- Lauren: provision dedicated tenant + schedule eval run (day 1 = once logs received)
- Marissa: assist with benchmark configs and quant profiles (cc'd)

I'll block the 11/19 10am PT slot on my calendar. Looking forward to the run.

Best,
Lauren

--
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Sounds good  we'll upload the sanitized logs to the HubSpot deal by EOD today and confirm the tenant requirements in the doc. Procurement will want the itemized estimate, so please include that in the bench PDF.

One last ask: can you include a short section in the report that maps open-candidate failure modes to likely mitigation (e.g., prompt engineering, dynamic reranking, or fallback to redwood-prod-v1)? That will help our engineers triage.

See you on 11/19 10am PT.

Thanks,
Evan
